findings.source_passage: “The master’s body?” roared the butler into the mouthpiece. “I’m sorry, madame, but we can’t furnish it—it’s far too hot to touch this noon!”
findings.source_locator: early visit to Buchanan house, telephone scene
findings.why_it_matters: Nick’s ironic gloss on the overheard call sets the chapter’s comic-surreal register and the heat motif; cutting it flattens both atmosphere and narrative voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full overheard line and Nick’s parenthetical clarification before the butler takes their hats.

findings.source_passage: In this heat every extra gesture was an affront to the common store of life.
findings.why_it_matters: This aphoristic sentence is classic Nick—compressed irony that critics quote when discussing Fitzgerald’s style. Losing it dulls the heat motif and narrator voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert the line verbatim after the butler ushers Nick and Gatsby inside.

findings.source_passage: “Do you mean you’ve been to a medium?” inquired Jordan humorously.  “What?  Confused, he stared at us as we laughed.  “A medium?”
findings.source_locator: drive to New York, Tom’s ‘second sight’ ramble
findings.why_it_matters: Jordan’s teasing and Tom’s bafflement are a rhythm break that exposes Tom’s pomposity; critics note the scene for its comic pacing. Its removal smooths away character shading.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-insert Jordan’s quip and Tom’s confused reaction before the ‘About Gatsby!’ exchange.

summary: Three voice-defining passages—telephone farce, heat aphorism, and Jordan’s ‘medium’ tease—are missing, warranting a regeneration pass.
